page: Microsoft Azure D4plds_v5 is an ARM-based virtual machine configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs and 8.0 GB of memory, yielding a 1:2 core-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The instance is powered by Ampere ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 physical cores operating at 3.0 GHz, backed by 64 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. It includes 161 GB of bundled local SSD temporary storage and operates on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor without discrete GPU acceleration.

Benchmark evaluations position the Ampere Neoverse-N1 processor within the middle tier for raw CPU execution, achieving 1822.38 in single-core stress-ng and 7232.57 in multi-core stress-ng workloads. However, instruction-intensive benchmarks register in lower tiers, with Geekbench recording 1112.0 single-core and 3670.0 multi-core scores. Cryptographic and extended instruction tasks show performance bottlenecks, evidenced by a Passmark CPU encryption result of 653.26 and a Passmark memory score of 1071.92.

Memory throughput is mixed; while 16 KB cached reads achieve 283.11 GB/sec, uncached 256 MB reads and writes maintain steady throughput at 49.0 GB/sec and 30.16 GB/sec respectively. Passmark database operations score at an average 2832.53, while Redis SET operations sustain 5.68 million operations per second and static web throughput reaches 5.83 GB/sec.

From a resource and efficiency perspective, the reduced memory footprint provides a lean operational model for compute-bound tasks that do not demand extensive memory caching. The integrated 161 GB NVMe SSD supplies rapid scratch space. Microsoft Azure D4plds_v5 is appropriate for lightweight scale-out microservices, CI/CD compilation, distributed application workers, and web serving.
description: Microsoft Azure D4plds_v5 is a compute-focused ARM64 virtual machine featuring 4 dedicated Ampere Neoverse-N1 cores clocked at 3.0 GHz, paired with 8.0 GB of RAM (2.0 GB per core) and 161 GB of bundled local SSD storage. Evaluated across standard synthetic suites, the instance demonstrates mid-tier CPU throughput in stress-ng tests (7232.57 multi-core) and large-block memory transfers (49.0 GB/sec read), while showing lower-tier performance in Geekbench (3670.0 multi-core) and hardware-accelerated encryption. With balanced single-thread per core allocation and dedicated local storage, the instance is technically tailored for scale-out microservices, containerized API workers, code build pipelines, and stateless web tiers.
